review.headline: A Petrov Three Knights where 15...Nb6?? and 16...e4?? undid a good opening

sections.text: You played the Petrov with 3...d6 and 4...Be6. After 5.Bb5+ c6 6.Ba4 b5 7.Bb3 a5 8.a4 b4 you gained queenside space, and 9...Bxb3 traded off White's bishop (10.cxb3). The position was balanced.

15.exd5? was a mistake by White (+1.6), but you replied with 15...Nb6??, which turned the position around (-0.9). 15...cxd5 simply took the pawn. Then 16...e4?? dropped to -3.0; 16...Rc8 was the solid move.

After 17...Qxd1+?! the queens came off with check and you were behind. White's 19.Rd6 and 20.Nd2? gave you small chances, but 21...Rac8? and 24...Be5? kept you from regaining control, and White's c-pawn on 22.c7 was a constant threat.
29 moves of fighting chess, but the game was decided by those two moves on 15 and 16.

review.turning_point: 15...Nb6?? turned a fine position into a worse one, and 16...e4?? added to it (-0.9 to -3.0).
review.focus: At 15...Nb6, look for the simple recapture. 15...cxd5 kept everything protected.

review.headline: A fast Italian attack that ended with 17.Qxg7#

sections.text: You played the main line of the Italian with 3.Bc4, 4.c3, 5.d4 and 6.cxd4, and after 6...Bb4+ 7.Nc3 Bxc3+ 8.bxc3 you had a healthy centre. Black's 8...d6? lost a bit of ground (+2.6).
You didn't play the most precise moves. 9.Ba3? and 10.O-O?? were slightly inaccurate, since 9.Ng5 and 10.Ng5 were more testing, hitting f7 right away. But the position was still better for you.
You kept control with 12.Qd2, 13.c4 and 14.d5, gaining space and driving Black's pieces back with 14...Na7. 15.Bb2 and 16.Qd4 aimed everything at the kingside.
Black's 16...c5?? was the final mistake, and you found 17.Qxg7# immediately, checkmate on g7. A tidy finish and a good example of lining up queen and bishop on the long diagonal.

review.turning_point: 16...c5?? allowed 17.Qxg7# along the long diagonal, and you spotted it at once.
review.focus: At 10.O-O, compare with 10.Ng5. When Black's king is not yet safe, pressure f7 before you finish development.

review.headline: A short Winawer where a queen raid with 10...Qg2! won on the clock

sections.text: As Black against 1.d4 you chose 2...e6 and 3...Bb4 against 3.e4, a Winawer-style setup. White pushed with 4.e5 and you challenged it with 4...f6, which is a principled reply. 6...fxe5 took the pawn and 7.Nxe5 recaptured.

7...Nxd4?! grabbed a pawn and was a little risky, but 8.Bd3?? was White's blunder; 8.Qh5+ was the stronger move. You answered with 8...Qh4?, which was a mistake (+0.8 to -0.5). 8...Nf6 was the calmer alternative.

White then went wrong again: 9.g3 Qh3 and 10.Nf3?? let you play 10...Qg2!, the best reply, attacking the rook on h1 and giving you a clear advantage at +2.9. 10.Nb5 was the better try. White ran out of time soon after.

review.turning_point: 10...Qg2! punished 10.Nf3?? and left White with a bad position; the clock decided the game.
review.focus: At 8...Qh4, you went queen-first before developing. 8...Nf6 would have been a more solid developing move.
